title: The Whole Team
logline: Before sunrise, a crew of a dozen people pulls a single net from two directions at once; no one could do any part of it alone, and the catch belongs to all of them the moment it is decided.
human_question: When something can only be done by everyone at once, whose achievement is it?

situation.what_happens: A crew sets one end of a very long net out on the water while the rest hold the other end, and then the whole group hauls for as long as it takes. Every person has a different job and none of the jobs is the work. The pull begins together and finishes together. When the net closes, what is in it is divided by an arrangement the crew already knows.
situation.who_is_involved: A crew who work together habitually, including older members who no longer haul but still take a share; the households the shares go to.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A morning's income for everyone at once, and an arrangement about sharing that has to survive a bad haul. For the film, the risk of turning precarious labour into a pleasing shape.
situation.how_it_unfolds: The work has one long movement — setting, hauling, closing, dividing — and it either produces something or it does not. Its pressures are weather, declining stocks, equipment cost and the fairness of the split. Reality decides what comes up in the net and what is said while it is divided.

concept_merge.why_together: C019's four marks of association — factors arise together, cease together, take the same object and rest on the same base, each with its own function — are almost exactly a crew that launches and lands as one; the digest itself reaches for a boat's crew as its image. C023 adds that the ease and coordination of a practised group is what workability and proficiency look like from outside.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the tradition's account of a mind is closer to a crew than to a person: distinct jobs, one object, one beginning and one end, and no member who is the work.

concept_links.why: The four marks describe factors that arise together, cease together, take the same object and depend on the same base, each with a distinct function [C019-P:L33-L47; C019-M:L3-L17]; the digest's own simile for this is a boat's crew that launches and lands together.
Workability and proficiency describe what repeated, shared effort makes possible, and the source's account of practice is that what is often done becomes easy [C023-P:L153-L157].

what_the_viewer_could_understand: A mind, in this account, is never a single thing acting alone: it is a set of qualities that begin together, attend to the same thing and finish together, each doing a different job.
what_must_be_real: The crew's actual livelihood, a real haul and a real division of what it produces. No repeat of the pull for the camera and no arranged catch.
position_hint: middle: it is an explanatory film about how a mind is put together, which needs the viewer to have seen good minds in action first.
risks: Turning hard, precarious labour into a pretty metaphor
Letting visual composition lead instead of the crew's own livelihood and words
drop_if: No crew is willing to have a real working morning filmed as it happens

connections.note: Its substance now lives inside IDEA-0095: work that exists only when several people begin and finish it together, carrying the four marks of association.

selection.reason: Shares both concepts with IDEA-0095 and duplicates it as physical-labour film; its four-marks image is stronger folded into that film than competing with it for a slot.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
